description: Bayesian fine-mapping of a GWAS locus via deep variational inference (PyTorch MLP training on CPU, 8000 iterations, 400 variants).
prompt: Perform Bayesian statistical fine-mapping of a GWAS locus for type 2 diabetes risk to identify the most probable causal genetic variant. Generate synthetic GWAS summary statistics for 400 variants as follows (numpy seed 7): label the variants rs_0 through rs_399; designate rs_250 as the single true causal variant with effect_size=0.35 and se=0.07; for the 20 nearest tag variants (rs_240 to rs_260, excluding rs_250) set effect_size drawn from N(0.18, 0.03) to simulate LD-induced association; for all remaining 379 variants set effect_size drawn from N(0.0, 0.04) with se=0.07; compute p-values for all variants from two-sided z-tests (z = effect_size / se). Build a 400×400 LD matrix with a block-diagonal structure: 4 blocks of 100 variants each where the within-block correlation decays as r_{ij} = 0.7^|i-j| (use scipy.linalg.toeplitz), and set between-block entries to 0.02. Save the summary statistics to 'gwas_t2d_locus.csv' with columns [variant_id, effect_size, pvalue, se]. Then call bayesian_finemapping_with_deep_vi from biomni.tool.genetics with n_iterations=8000, hidden_dim=128, credible_threshold=0.95. Report: (1) the top 10 variants ranked by posterior inclusion probability (PIP), (2) the total number of variants in the 95% credible set, (3) whether rs_250 (the true causal variant) appears in the 95% credible set and its rank by PIP.
notes: Calls biomni.tool.genetics.bayesian_finemapping_with_deep_vi which trains a small PyTorch MLP (two hidden layers of size hidden_dim=128) using variational inference for 8000 iterations. Runs entirely on CPU because the function uses torch.FloatTensor (CPU) without calling .cuda(). Expected execute_total_s: 20-90s depending on PyTorch optimization speed. Expected GPU bubble: 40-70%. The function requires the datetime module and torch/nn at import time. The agent must create the GWAS CSV file before calling the function, and must pass the LD matrix as a numpy array (not a path). The Toeplitz LD structure r_{ij}=0.7^|i-j| gives a realistic exponentially decaying LD pattern; within-block variants near rs_250 will have elevated PIPs, making it a good test of the fine-mapping algorithm's ability to distinguish causal from tag variants.
